title: Deontic statement
description: A norm transcribed into a deontic formula: an operator over a (bearer : action) pair, with optional condition and exception. Structured projection of the canonical grammar. No inference is implied.

operator.description: The deontic modality: O obligation, P permission, F prohibition. "Right" is not a modality — it is a Hohfeldian incident (see incident).

condition.description: Applicability antecedent; non-empty makes the norm conditional.

exception.description: Defeasibility carve-out; non-empty makes the norm defeasible.

exception_status.description: The classification of `exception`'s own text (deontic.prose_grammar.classify_exception_status): whether an exception clause was detected at all, and — when one was — whether it resolved to local text or names an unresolved cross-reference / external law. '' only when the producer does not classify one (a formula built directly, bypassing prose/classify_exception_status); every prose-derived statement carries one of the four typed values, never bare.

negated.description: True when the operator scopes a negative proposition (¬action).

incident.description: The Hohfeldian position the norm creates, from the addressee's perspective. '' = not classified (abstention, never a guess).

counterparty.description: The correlative role (claim-holder / party exposed to a power) when the norm names it.

deadline.description: Optional, additive. The time by which the norm bites, as opaque text (e.g. "within 24 hours", "by 31 December 2026"). Carried, not typed or scheduled — the reasoning layer types it. '' = none.

cross_references.description: Optional, additive. Instruments this norm points to, as opaque text (e.g. "Article 43", "§ 22 BDSG"). Carried, not resolved. [] = none.

sanction.description: Optional, additive. The consequence attached to breach, as opaque text (e.g. "a fine up to EUR 20 000 000"). Carried, not applied. '' = none.
